trace.msg: Let's look at this puzzle carefully. I'll only move when I can explain why.
I can't rule out around the edge to (1,1) or around the edge to (5,5) yet, so I'll make an educated guess: around the edge to (1,1).
Going right, the next move is forced and the line gets stuck at cell (1,3). So the line goes around the edge to (1,5).

Contradiction! Every way forward fails: going to number 2, every way of continuing runs into a dead end within a few moves; going down would leave number 2 unreachable without crossing a higher number; going around the edge to (5,5), every way of continuing runs into a dead end within a few moves. So my guess (around the edge to (1,1) from number 1) was wrong, so the line must go around the edge to (5,5).
I can't rule out around the edge to (1,5) or left yet, so I'll make an educated guess: around the edge to (1,5).
Going down would leave number 2 unreachable without crossing a higher number; going around the edge to (1,1), the next 2 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at cell (1,3). So the line goes left.
Going around the edge to (5,4) would leave number 3 unreachable without crossing a higher number. So the line goes left.
Number 3 is only reachable this way.
Going down, every way of continuing runs into a dead end within a few moves. So the line goes left.
Going down would leave number 5 unreachable without crossing a higher number; going up, the next move is forced and the line gets stuck at cell (1,1). So the line goes left.
Cell (1,1) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes up.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes right.
Cell (5,4) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes right.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes up.
Going up would force the line onto number 10 before its turn; going left, the next move is forced and the line gets stuck at cell (3,3). So the line goes right.
Number 9 is next and right here, so the line takes it.
Cell (2,5) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes up.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes left.
Cell (4,3) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes down.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes left.
Every cell is covered and the numbers are in order. Case closed!
I grow a search tree: my policy network suggests moves, a trained value head judge them. 40 simulations per move.
One of my simulated futures reached the end after 13 simulations. Following it!
Let evolution do the work: 24 random lines compete, the fittest breed and mutate.
Generation 0: the best random line covers 8/25 cells (32%).
Generation 1: fitness 8/25. The best line covers 12 cells, the first 8 of them still look solvable.
Generation 5: fitness 14/25. The best line covers 20 cells, the first 14 of them still look solvable.
Generation 6: fitness 25/25. The best line covers 25 cells.
Generation 6: a perfect line evolved! Every cell covered.
Feeling lucky! Before every move I'll play 24 random futures and bet on the move that survives most often.
Jackpot! A future after going around the edge to (5,5) covers the whole board. Cashing in!
Let x(cell, step) mean 'this cell is step number <step> of the line'. 25 cells x 25 steps, minus everything that's impossible at a glance.
Encoded 1,373 variables and 3,724 clauses in 0.07 s (379 position variables survive the pruning).
Solver found a model in 0.00 s. Decoding it into a line...
Q.E.D. Every clause is satisfied.
